questions.topic: Operator Precedence — Difference Between *p + 1 and *(p + 1)
questions.q: What is expression *p + 1 equal to if p points to first element a[0] for array int a[3] = {1, 2, 3}?
questions.hint: Which operator has higher precedence — dereference * or addition +?
explanations: Correct! Dereference operator * has higher precedence than +. Expression *p first reads value a[0] (1), and then adds 1. Total: 1 + 1 = 2.
Incorrect. 1 is just value *p without adding one.
Incorrect. 3 would be obtained with *(p + 2) or *p + 2.
Incorrect. Expression is completely valid.

questions.topic: sizeof Operator — Size of Single Row of 2D Array
questions.q: What is sizeof(a[0]) equal to for matrix int a[2][3] given a 4-byte int?
questions.hint: How many int elements does first row a[0] contain?
explanations: Correct! a[0] is the first row of a 2D array containing 3 int elements. Calculating 3 * 4 yields 12 bytes.
Incorrect. 24 bytes (2 * 3 * 4) is size of entire matrix sizeof(a).
Incorrect. 4 bytes is size of single element a[0][0].
Incorrect. 8 bytes is pointer size on 64-bit architecture.

questions.topic: Pointers and Strings — Character Array Subscripting via Pointer
questions.q: Which character will expression *(p + 2) output for char a[] = "ABC" and char *p = a?
questions.hint: Calculate character at offset + 2 from start of string.
explanations: Correct! p + 2 shifts pointer by 2 positions right, pointing to 'C' (index 2). Dereferencing *(p + 2) returns character 'C'. Equivalent to a[2].
Incorrect. 'B' is at offset *(p + 1).
Incorrect. 'A' is at initial address *p.
Incorrect. Null terminator is at offset *(p + 3).

questions.topic: Pointer Arithmetic — Subtracting Pointers to Elements of Same Array
questions.q: What is difference p - a equal to if p = &a[2] for array int a[4]?
questions.hint: In what units is difference between two pointers to elements of same array calculated?
explanations: Correct! p points to element at index 2, while a decays to pointer to element at index 0. Subtracting two pointers of same type returns count of elements between them: 2 - 0 = 2.
Incorrect. 8 bytes would be obtained only with explicit pointer casting to char*.
Incorrect. 4 is total element count in array a.
Incorrect. Pointer subtraction within same array is strictly regulated by standard.

questions.topic: Memory — Flat Access to 2D Array via int*
questions.q: What is element p[2] equal to upon explicit cast of matrix int a[2][2] = {1, 2, 3, 4} to int*?
questions.hint: Recall memory layout order of matrix elements (Row-Major Order).
explanations: Correct! 2D array lies continuously in memory: a[0][0] (1), a[0][1] (2), a[1][0] (3), a[1][1] (4). Pointer p[2] requests element with flat index 2, which is a[1][0], equal to 3.
Incorrect. 1 is p[0] element (a[0][0]).
Incorrect. 2 is p[1] element (a[0][1]).
Incorrect. 4 is p[3] element (a[1][1]).

questions.topic: sizeof Operator — Comparing Array Size and Pointer Size
questions.q: What will sizeof(a) == sizeof(a + 0) output on a 64-bit system with 4-byte int for int a[3]?
questions.hint: What are sizeof(a) (array) and sizeof(a + 0) (pointer expression) equal to?
explanations: Correct! sizeof(a) returns full array size (3 * 4 = 12 bytes). In expression a + 0, array name loses its array type and decays to pointer int*, whose sizeof on a 64-bit system is 8 bytes. 12 == 8 is false, so result is 0.
Incorrect. Sizes are not equal (12 != 8).
Incorrect. Comparison is valid from type and syntax perspective.
Incorrect. Operator sizeof is evaluated at compile time.

questions.topic: Operator Precedence — Prefix Increment of Dereferenced Value ++*p
questions.q: What will printf("%d", ++*p) output for int a[3] = {5, 10, 15} and int *p = a?
questions.hint: What exactly does prefix increment ++*p increase — address or value?
explanations: Correct! Operators ++ (prefix) and * have same precedence and right-to-left associativity. Expression parses as ++(*p). First a[0] (5) is dereferenced, then incremented by 1 to 6 and printed.
Incorrect. 5 would be printed without ++ operator.
Incorrect. 10 is value of a[1], but pointer p itself does not shift.
Incorrect. 11 would be obtained by incrementing element a[1].

questions.topic: Initialization — Default Values for Uninitialized Elements
questions.q: What is element a[3] equal to upon partial initialization int a[5] = {1, 2, 3}?
questions.hint: What happens to remainder of array if initializer list has fewer elements than array size?
explanations: Correct! Under C standard, if initializer list is specified for at least one element, all remaining unspecified elements are guaranteed zeroed. a[3] equals 0.
Incorrect. 3 is element a[2].
Incorrect. Garbage remains only in completely UNinitialized automatic arrays.
Incorrect. Partial initialization is standard C mechanics.

questions.topic: 2D Arrays — Dereferencing Row a[1]
questions.q: What is value *a[1] equal to for matrix int a[2][3] = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}?
questions.hint: Which element does a[1] point to as base pointer of its row?
explanations: Correct! a[1] points to start of second row {4, 5, 6}. Dereferencing *a[1] is equivalent to a[1][0], yielding value 4.
Incorrect. 1 is first element of matrix a[0][0] (*a[0]).
Incorrect. 2 is element a[0][1].
Incorrect. 3 is element a[0][2].

questions.topic: sizeof Operator — Fixed-Length char Array Size
questions.q: What is sizeof(str) equal to for declaration char str[10] = "Hi"?
questions.hint: Does sizeof compute physical memory size of array or length of string contained within it?
explanations: Correct! Operator sizeof returns total memory allocated for array, namely 10 bytes (char[10]). String length (2) is returned by strlen function.
Incorrect. 2 is result of strlen(str) excluding '\0'.
Incorrect. 3 is string length including null terminator.
Incorrect. 8 is char* pointer size.

questions.topic: Pointers — Zero Index of Shifted Pointer p[0]
questions.q: What is value p[0] equal to if pointer p is initialized as a + 1 for int a[3] = {10, 20, 30}?
questions.hint: Which element of array a does p point to at shift a + 1?
explanations: Correct! p points to a[1] (value 20). Expression p[0] expands to *(p + 0), reading element at current address a[1], which is 20.
Incorrect. 10 is a[0] (or p[-1]).
Incorrect. 30 is a[2] (or p[1]).
Incorrect. Reading element a[1] is completely valid.

questions.topic: Syntax — Equivalence of a[1] and *(a + 1)
questions.q: What is expression *(a + 1) equal to for array int a[3] = {1, 2, 3}?
questions.hint: Which array element corresponds to this classic dereferencing notation?
explanations: Correct! By C syntax definition, expression *(a + i) is strictly identical to a[i]. For i = 1, this is second element a[1], equal to 2.
Incorrect. 1 is element a[0] (*(a + 0)).
Incorrect. 3 is element a[2] (*(a + 2)).
Incorrect. Notation is foundational for array handling in C.

questions.topic: Initialization — Zero Elements in Nested Initializer Lists
questions.q: What is element a[0][1] equal to for matrix int a[2][2] = {{10}, {20, 30}}?
questions.hint: Check number of specified elements in first subarray {10}.
explanations: Correct! First row subarray {10} explicitly specifies only a[0][0] = 10. Second element of this row a[0][1] has no explicit value and is automatically zeroed (0).
Incorrect. 10 is element a[0][0].
Incorrect. 20 is element a[1][0].
Incorrect. Omitted slots in partially initialized array are automatically zeroed.

questions.topic: Assignment Operators — Compound Pointer Assignment +=
questions.q: What will printf("%d", *(p += 2)) output for int a[3] = {1, 2, 3} and int *p = a?
questions.hint: Which element will pointer p shift to after executing p += 2?
explanations: Correct! Expression p += 2 adds 2 elements to address p, moving it to a[2]. Expression returns updated pointer, dereferencing * which yields value of a[2], equal to 3.
Incorrect. 1 is initial element a[0].
Incorrect. 2 is element a[1] upon p += 1.
Incorrect. Compound assignment += is permitted for pointers.

questions.topic: Pointer Arithmetic — Subtracting Element Addresses of Character Array
questions.q: What is difference &a[4] - &a[1] equal to for array char a[] = "12345"?
questions.hint: Calculate index difference between two array elements.
explanations: Correct! Subtracting two pointers of same type returns count of elements of that type between them: 4 - 1 = 3. Since char element type takes 1 byte, difference is 3.
Incorrect. 4 is value of index 4 itself.
Incorrect. 1 is value of index 1 itself.
Incorrect. 12 is erroneous value from incorrect multiplication by type size.

questions.topic: sizeof Operator — Comparing sizeof(a) and sizeof(&a)
questions.q: What will printf output given 4-byte int and 64-bit pointers?
questions.hint: Remember sizeof(a) evaluates size of whole array, while sizeof(&a) evaluates size of pointer to array.
explanations: Correct! sizeof(a) returns total size of 10-element int array: 10 * 4 = 40 bytes. Expression &a yields type 'pointer to array' (int(*)[10]), whose size on 64-bit platform is 8 bytes. Output: "40 8".
Incorrect. &a is a pointer, so its sizeof is 8 bytes, not 40.
Incorrect. a in sizeof(a) does not decay to pointer, returning size of allocated array (40).
Incorrect. 4 is size of single int element.

questions.topic: Pointers to Arrays — Dereferencing (*p)[1]
questions.q: What is result of expression (*p)[1], where p is a pointer to entire array int (*p)[3] = &a?
questions.hint: Dereferencing *p yields array a itself. Which element will subsequent subscripting [1] return?
explanations: Correct! p stores address of entire array &a. Operation *p dereferences it back into array a. Expression (*p)[1] reads second array element, equal to 20.
Incorrect. 10 is first element (*p)[0].
Incorrect. 30 is third element (*p)[2].
Incorrect. Syntax int (*p)[N] is completely correct.

questions.topic: Operator Precedence — Incrementing Value via Pointer (*p)++
questions.q: What will element a[0] equal after executing command (*p)++?
questions.hint: Do parentheses (*p) specify retrieving value of first array element prior to increment?
explanations: Correct! Parentheses force order: first *p is dereferenced, giving access to slot a[0] (value 10). Operator ++ increments value of this slot by 1, so a[0] becomes 11.
Incorrect. 10 is value prior to increment execution.
Incorrect. 20 is element a[1], but pointer p itself was not modified.
Incorrect. Second slot a[1] remains unchanged.

questions.topic: Pointers — Negative Index p[-2] from Array Middle
questions.q: What is expression p[-2] equal to if p points to a[3]?
questions.hint: Step 2 elements back from index 3.
explanations: Correct! p stores address &a[3]. Indexing p[-2] is equivalent to *(p - 2). Stepping 2 elements back leads to slot a[1], storing number 20.
Incorrect. 10 is element a[0] (p[-3]).
Incorrect. 30 is element a[2] (p[-1]).
Incorrect. Address of slot a[1] is within array bounds.

questions.topic: Character Arrays — Explicit List Initialization of Elements
questions.q: Which character will printf output when printing a[2] for char a[3] = {'A', 'B', 'C'}?
questions.hint: From which index does array element numbering start?
explanations: Correct! Array is initialized with three characters at indices 0, 1, and 2. a[2] corresponds to last element — character 'C'. Specifier %c will print 'C'. (Note: there is no null terminator in this array).
Incorrect. 'B' is at index a[1].
Incorrect. 'A' is at index a[0].
Incorrect. Array consists of exactly three specified characters.

questions.topic: 2D Arrays — Double Dereferencing **a
questions.q: What is value **a equal to for 2D array int a[2][3] = {{1, 2, 3}, {4, 5, 6}}?
questions.hint: What value will be obtained upon first and second dereference of 2D array name?
explanations: Correct! First dereference *a yields pointer to first subarray a[0]. Second dereference **a yields first element of first subarray a[0][0], equal to 1.
Incorrect. 4 is element *a[1] (a[1][0]).
Incorrect. 2 is element a[0][1].
Incorrect. Double dereferencing for 2D array is completely valid.

questions.topic: Arithmetic — Adding Results of Dereferencing *p + *p
questions.q: What is result of expression *p + *p equal to if p points to a[0] for int a[3] = {10, 20, 30}?
questions.hint: Do dereferences shift pointer p?
explanations: Correct! Expression *p takes value of first slot a[0], equal to 10. Repeated call *p reads 10 again. 10 + 10 = 20. Pointer p does not change its address during this.
Incorrect. 30 would be obtained with *p + *(p + 1) (10 + 20).
Incorrect. 40 would be obtained with *(p + 1) + *(p + 1).
Incorrect. Plus operator sums two tens.

questions.topic: Function Parameters — Passing Array and Subscripting Inside Function
questions.q: What will call print_val(arr) output for int arr[3] = {5, 15, 25}?
questions.hint: Which element is selected by index a[1] inside function?
explanations: Correct! Array arr is passed to function by pointer a. Inside function a[1] takes second array element (index 1), equal to 15.
Incorrect. 5 is element a[0].
Incorrect. 25 is element a[2].
Incorrect. Passing array as int a[] is syntactically valid.

questions.topic: Strings — Array Size Calculation with Implicit and Explicit Zeros
questions.q: What is sizeof(a) equal to for character array char a[] = "A\0B"?
questions.hint: Count all bytes of string literal, including explicit \0 and trailing null terminator.
explanations: Correct! String literal consists of characters 'A', '\0', 'B' and hidden automatic null terminator '\0' at literal end. Total array takes exactly 4 bytes in memory.
Incorrect. 3 would be obtained if compiler did not add trailing '\0'.
Incorrect. 2 is result of strlen(a) only up to first '\0', but sizeof computes entire array volume.
Incorrect. sizeof sees entire volume of initializer.

questions.topic: Structures — Pointer Arithmetic on Structure Array (p + 1)->y
questions.q: What is expression (p + 1)->y equal to for structure array struct Point arr[2] = {{1, 2}, {3, 4}}?
questions.hint: Which structure does p + 1 point to and what is its y member?
explanations: Correct! p points to arr[0]. Shift p + 1 moves to second structure arr[1]. Operator ->y reads its y field, equal to 4.
Incorrect. 2 is y field of first structure arr[0].y (p->y).
Incorrect. 3 is x field of second structure arr[1].x ((p + 1)->x).
Incorrect. 1 is x field of first structure.

questions.topic: Arrays of Pointers — Accessing Value *arr[0]
questions.q: What will printf output when dereferencing *arr[0] for pointer array int *arr[1] = {&x}?
questions.hint: What is stored at index arr[0] and what value will its dereference return?
explanations: Correct! arr[0] contains pointer &x. Dereferencing *arr[0] returns value stored in variable x, which is 42.
Incorrect. Address would be returned when calling arr[0] without * sign.
Incorrect. Pointer arrays are initialized with variable addresses without errors.
Incorrect. Variable x stores 42.

questions.topic: Constants — Reading Constant Array via Pointer const int *p
questions.q: What is expression *(p + 2) equal to for array const int a[3] = {10, 20, 30}?
questions.hint: Does const qualifier forbid reading array elements?
explanations: Correct! Qualifier const forbids only MODIFICATION (writing) of data. Reading from array is allowed. Expression *(p + 2) reads third element a[2], equal to 30.
Incorrect. 10 is element a[0] (*p).
Incorrect. 20 is element a[1] (*(p + 1)).
Incorrect. Reading constants is completely legal.

questions.topic: Pointer Arithmetic — Address Difference &a[4] - a
questions.q: What is difference &a[4] - a equal to for array int a[5]?
questions.hint: In what units is difference between pointer to element and array base pointer measured?
explanations: Correct! Array name a decays to pointer to its first element &a[0]. Subtraction &a[4] - &a[0] returns index difference: 4 - 0 = 4 elements.
Incorrect. 16 bytes would be obtained with explicit casting of both pointers to char*.
Incorrect. 5 is total element count in array.
Incorrect. Difference of same-type pointers is not automatically converted to bytes.

questions.topic: Initialization — Incomplete Traditional Array Initialization in C89
questions.q: What will printf output when calculating sums a[0] + a[1] and a[2] + a[3] for int a[4] = {1, 2}?
questions.hint: What are values of elements a[2] and a[3] if initializer list contains only 2 numbers?
explanations: Correct! Explicitly specified elements: a[0] = 1, a[1] = 2. All unspecified array elements in C are guaranteed zeroed: a[2] = 0, a[3] = 0. First expression: 1 + 2 = 3, second: 0 + 0 = 0. Output: "3 0".
Incorrect. a[2] and a[3] do not duplicate previous values, but fill with zeros.
Incorrect. With list initialization present, no garbage remains in elements.
Incorrect. Partial array initialization fully complies with C89/C90.

questions.topic: Memory — Equality of Matrix Address a and First Element Address &a[0][0]
questions.q: What will comparison (void*)a == (void*)&a[0][0] output for 2D array int a[2][2]?
questions.hint: Does start address of entire matrix match address of its very first element?
explanations: Correct! Array is located in memory as a single block. Address of array a itself, address of its first row &a[0], and address of first element &a[0][0] point to same memory cell. Comparison returns 1 (true).
Incorrect. Addresses are guaranteed equal.
Incorrect. Casting to (void*) correctly matches pointers.
Incorrect. Behavior of comparing object start addresses is strictly defined.
